newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia pays out 185 mln dinars farmers debt -paper.
newsitem.headline: Serbia pays out 185 mln dinars farmers debt -paper.

text.p: The Serbian government has to date cleared 185 million of 800 million dinars ($147.5 million) of its outstanding farmers debt for 1996 crops, Belgrade daily Politika reported on Tuesday.
The federal government is expected to secure another 50 million dinars and the central bank 200 million, the paper quoted Serbian agriculture minister Jovan Babovic as saying.
"About 45 million dinars was paid out in cash, 30 million in commodities and 111 million in exchange for semi-finished goods necessary for spring planting," Babovic said.
The remaining 400 million dinars are owed by the food processing industry which is negotiating ways of repaying it, the minister said.
Enough seeds, herbicides, fuel and about 600,000 tonnes of fertilisers have already been secured for the spring planting planned on 2.37 million hectares.

About three billion dinars is needed for financing the entire spring sowing, Babovic said. Babovic added, "the structure and the size of the spring campaign entirely depend on clearing the farmers' debt."

Out of the total area planned for spring planting, 1.4 million was planned to be sown with maize, 100,000 with sugar beet, 200,000 with sunflower, 80,000 with soybean, 255,000 with vegetables and 190,000 with fodder crops.
-- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom ++381 11 222 4254 ($ = 5.423 Yugoslav Dinars)
